SUMMARY OF THE RISP SCIENCE PROGRAM
The accomplishment of the stated objectives of RISP depends on the integrated science program which has been proposed. The discussion which follows attempts to outline the kinds of research that will be a part of the RISP science operations. More complete discussions of these scientific studies are contained in following sections of this plan.
Geophysical Investigations 
The objectives of the geophysical program in connection with RISP can be divided into four general categories: 1) survey of ice thickness and water depth for drill site selection; 2) studies of the physical properties of the ice shelf; 3) measurement of the ocean tide by means of recording tidal gravimeters; and 4) studies of the underlying geologic structures.
It is recognized that only a portion of the proposed geophysical program might be said to be directly related to RISP. However, the Steering Group also recognizes the need for some understanding of the regional setting as an aid to the interpretation of the data obtained at the drill site. Some excellent information is available (see for example Crary 1961a, 1961b; Crary and others, 1962; and Bennett, 1964) and has been utilized in the selection of a tentative drill site for RISP. The radio-echo sounding maps prepared by Robin (pers. comm., 1972) and by the U.S.G.S.
